requirement:
Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.

The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
rationale:
**Confirmation:** the assessments disagreed

First assessment `true`: I found no test-adequacy gap in the reviewed tests for `requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`. All of them are in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs`. I did not read the implementation.

- **80% target on exact counts.** `mod[tests]/fn[exact_per_file_threshold_and_partial_functions]` asserts `threshold(79_999,100_000)` is false and `threshold(80_000,100_000)` is true. It also asserts `threshold(0,0)` is false and that 4/5 passes. This covers the exact-count requirement against a rounded 80.0% display.
- **No averaging across files.** The same test fails `driver.rs` at 0/1 even though the other file is at 100%. It fails `driver.rs` at 7/10 even though the average of 100% and 70% is 85%.
- **No 80% target within a function.** `a_function_below_eighty_percent_needs_no_exception_when_its_file_passes` has a function at 1/3 inside a file at 10/12. It asserts the report passes with no accepted exceptions.
- **Union rule.** `children_and_filtered_runs_contribute_to_the_same_union` combines a parent and a child process, which cover complementary lines. It asserts 5/5. A later run with zero counts does not erase earlier execution, so lines count once and any positive count covers them.
- **Freshness, selection and active build.** `stale_missing_legacy_and_invalid_store_cannot_use_older_success` covers these cases:
  - an older success cannot be reused;
  - a missing profile fails;
  - missing function attribution fails;
  - a changed source file is reported as stale;
  - a corrupt run or an unusable store version fails;
  - a newly activated `other-config` build with missing attribution is treated as unavailable.
- **Exception evidence.** `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution`, `missing_and_stale_explanations_fail_the_report`, and `function_explanations_never_transfer_to_other_functions_or_the_file` cover these cases:
  - a file below threshold passes only with an accepted exception;
  - a missing, false, FIXME or stale review fails;
  - a file exception does not excuse its functions.
- **Unmeasured executable files.** `unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear` has `code.rs` with `fn missing` and no recorded lines. It asserts `code.rs: not measured — FAIL`, so no percentage is fabricated. The accepted-explanations test shows `not measured — accepted exception` when an exception exists.
- **No obligations.** `unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear` also asserts that a file with only a struct and a trait declaration is reported `no executable obligations — pass`. `default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not` checks the inventory flag for declarations, macro calls and derives.
- **Missing lines do not mean no obligations.** The `not measured — FAIL` case above has no recorded lines but does have an executable function, so it is not classed as having no obligations. Cfg-excluded functions are also treated as obligations.
- **Parse failure.** `measured_file_threshold_remains_checked_when_source_parsing_fails` checks that the threshold still applies when a file's source fails to parse. A parse failure is reported and fails the check.

Every clause I identified has a test that exercises it and asserts the outcome. The tests that cover it carry `{test}` references to the subject.

Second assessment `false`: Add a threshold test in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs`, marked `{test}` for `requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`. It should check that a result from an inactive build configuration, and a stale result whose captured source differs from the current source, contribute no line counts to a file's exact numerator and denominator. Use otherwise valid results with full attribution. Example: the current-configuration result leaves `code.rs` at 0/1 or 3/5, and an older other-configuration result or a stale result shows the line as executed or 5/5. Assert `!result.passed`, and assert the FAIL line shows the current-only counts, such as `code.rs: 0/1 (0.0%) — FAIL`. The test must show that the stale or inactive higher coverage cannot rescue the file. — The subject says the check MUST use the selection and freshness rules, restricted to the active build configuration. Union and exact-count behaviour is well tested. That covers `exact_per_file_threshold_and_partial_functions`, which checks 79,999/100,000 fails and that an 85% average cannot rescue a 70% file. It also covers `children_and_filtered_runs_contribute_to_the_same_union`. Unmeasured files, files with no executable obligations, and a file with no recorded lines are covered by `unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear`, `default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not`, and `measured_file_threshold_remains_checked_when_source_parsing_fails`. The exception paths are covered by the explanation tests. The exclusion of stale or inactive-configuration results from the counts is not enforced anywhere, though. In `stale_missing_legacy_and_invalid_store_cannot_use_older_success`, the only other-configuration result (`old`) has `functions = None`, so the check fails because that result is unavailable. That does not show that its line counts are ignored. The stale-source case asserts only that the text contains `stale coverage`. It does not assert `!passed` or the resulting counts. An implementation could therefore add the lines of an inactive-configuration or stale result to the union and let a file clear 80%. That violates the requirement, and the reviewed tests would accept it.

Recorded the second assessment (`false`).

Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.
The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage.parsing
Repository validation parses every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs`
file among the sources reference discovery considers under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root
`vendor` directory. It reports a Rust parse failure rather than silently
skipping the file.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
:::{req} index.summary
Saved execution-coverage checks compute line coverage from the union of
instrumented file-and-line locations in the eligible current results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, including child processes.
Each location counts once in the denominator and is covered when any selected
process has a positive execution count. Percentages use these union counts,
rather than averaging process reports.
When the current set has no usable instrumented lines, or any current result
has unavailable measurements under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`, combined coverage is
reported as unavailable. The check does not publish measured coverage
percentages or threshold results computed from only the remaining readable
results. Otherwise, absent file or function measurements remain subject to
their coverage obligations.
:::{req} index.selection
Saved execution-coverage checks read the current coverage set under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.current` from SQLite. Each check
uses one coherent database snapshot of test identities, states, provenance,
and processed measurements, so a replacement or update cannot mix results
from different snapshots within the same check.
Checks do not search historical runs or use a separate report-selection
metadata cache. Current test identities, states, and provenance can be read
without loading their detailed measurements.
Only current results with complete, available measurements contribute to
coverage under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`.
Pending, running, and unavailable entries are reported under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`. Checking does not build
or execute tests and never restores a superseded attempt.
:::{req} index.freshness
Only current results whose captured source inputs match the current source
and whose build configurations are compatible contribute counts to saved
execution-coverage checks under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`. Results with changed
inputs are identified as stale; results of unknown compatibility are
identified as unavailable. Both are excluded from combined totals.
A filtered run preserves the provenance of unselected results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`. It does not make those
results fresh when their recorded inputs no longer match. Their process
reports and matching captured source remain available until replacement or
removal of the build artifacts.
